hypotheses.mechanism: About a quarter of the GT divisions we miss have no detected second daughter. In the final exp39 graph, 23 of the 132 missed GT divisions (approximate per-division 7 um matching, validated because the fork labels reproduce the official 23 TP / 43 FP exactly) have no node for the second daughter at t+1. At the ckpt stage 13 have none, and the tail deletes 10 more. Another 12 have the daughter only at t+2. B35 A0 gives a window-rule reach of 136/151 with the current detections. Friend A's full-frame pass at threshold 0.90 reaches 151/151, so the missing daughters exist as SUB-THRESHOLD peaks. This fits the known shrinkage of dividing nuclei (half-max volume -0.17..-0.27 at +1..+3 frames). The full-frame pass failed only on node budget (+24% nodes). Separately, in 17 of 54 'claimed' misses the node matched to GT daughter b sits more than 4 um from b (median 2.9 um). There the true daughter is probably undetected, and a recovered peak closer to b would take the 7 um match. Geometry alone cannot find these: in the orphan pool, midpoint, mirror and grandparent-centred features give 1-3% precision (112,975 candidate orphans, 30 TP / 2,537 FP). So the extra evidence must come from the detector heatmap, conditioned on a high parent score.
hypotheses.change: Kernel: in the predictor, after the 8-view TTA heatmap and 3 um NMS, keep a side table of peaks with 0.90 <= h < 0.965 that were not emitted as nodes (tiny, float coords; sub-voxel refined by the coord head once ported). Post-tail, inside div_insert as a new 'mirror' branch: for each single-child parent u (child c1 at t+1) with DaughterNet p_par(u) >= tau and no admissible orphan, search the side table at t+1 for x with sister(c1,x) in [6,14.5] um (GT p10-p90 6.4-14.4), |u-x| <= 11 um, cos(c1-u, x-u) <= 0.25, and |x-(2u-c1)| <= 5 um (mirror prior). Score = p_par(u) * p_dau(c1)^alpha * h(x) * exp(-|x-mirror|^2/2s^2). Insert greedily, cap 1-2 per video: add node x and edge u->x. If a free orphan start lies within 4 um of x at t+2, also add x->orphan (gap-style). Otherwise x is a one-node branch, which the official rule credits through direct-child evidence. The node term cost is ~1/25k per node.
hypotheses.upper_bound: Local: 15 GT divisions are unreachable under the window rule (151-136), plus up to 17 claimed-far cases, so 32/151 at most. Recovering all 15 at zero FP gives J 23/194 = 0.119 -> 38/194 = 0.196, i.e. +0.0077 score. Public: J_pub = 0.36 with an assumed D ~ 53 (TP ~19 / FP ~13 / FN ~21, a guess from J and typical precision). If 5 of about 50 public GT divisions are missing-daughter cases and all are recovered at zero FP, J = 24/53 = 0.45, i.e. +0.009 ceiling.
hypotheses.lab_test: Inputs: friend A's full-frame 0.90 peak cache from B35 step A (tools/recover_daughters.py, all 199 videos) as the side table; DaughterNet OOF p (data_external/l2/node_p_oof_v1v2avg.parquet, rescoring parents not in the 1M export via K-DN-score); the replay lab experiments/l2_daughternet/replay/replay.py with a new ins.mirror config. Run a SELECTION grid (tau p_par, cap 1/2/3, mirror radius 4/5/6 um, h floor 0.90/0.93), then ONE CONFIRMATION run on exp48-equivalent. Success: net division TP >= +4, added-fork precision >= 0.40 (public break-even 0.265 plus margin), score >= +0.002, each embryo >= +0.001, node ratio change < +0.05%.
hypotheses.expected_gain: Local: 8 added forks at precision 0.45 gives dJ ~ (q(1+J)-J)*n/D = (0.45*1.119-0.119)*8/194 = +0.016, i.e. +0.0016 score. Range +0.001..+0.003. Public: 3 added forks at q = 0.5 with J = 0.36 and D ~ 53 gives (0.68-0.36)*3/53 = +0.018 J, i.e. +0.0018 score. Range +0.001..+0.003.
hypotheses.transfer_risk: Medium. The public detector was trained on all 199 train videos, so sub-threshold peaks at training daughters may be stronger locally than on unseen embryos. That makes recall optimistic in the lab, while precision is set by the honest OOF DaughterNet. The threshold 0.90 and the mirror radius come from 6bba-dominated data. The inserted one-node branches must be added post-tail (after leaf pruning), or they get pruned.
hypotheses.not_closed_because: B35 step A closed a FULL-FRAME 0.90 pass on node budget (+24% nodes) and kept recovered nodes out of the submission. B32 closed the orphan-only pool on reach. This is a targeted, capped lookup: at most 1-3 nodes per video, only around parents already ranked by DaughterNet, with a sister-geometry prior. It is neither the pool nor the budget of the closed lines, and it is not a detector fine-tune or TTA change.

hypotheses.mechanism: Our false-positive forks are continuations of annotated, non-dividing cells: only 1 of the 43 local FP forks is near a GT division. Their parent does not sit between the two children. mid = |P - (c1+c2)/2| has median 3.0 um for FP forks vs 1.58 um for TP forks, and every one of the 23 TP forks has mid <= 3.8 um. The safe-division gates check |P-c1| <= 10, |P-v| <= 9, sister <= 14, mutual NN, divergence and the symmetry of |P-c1| vs |P-v|. None of them checks the midpoint or the angle, so 'continuation + neighbour on the same side' passes. DivNet cannot separate these forks: parent p median is 0.77 for TP vs 0.76 for FP, which is why the DivNet veto tied on the LB. Because J_pub (0.36) is much larger than local J (0.119), the lab under-values fork removal: break-even precision of the removed set is 0.265 on public vs 0.106 locally.
hypotheses.change: Post-tail, after safe-div and the DaughterNet insertion, never touching nodes: for every fork whose added edge is a safe-division or divinsert edge, drop that edge when mid >= 4.0 um (variant 3.5). The daughter becomes a track start again. Tighten div_insert mid_um from 6.5 to 4.0 so insertions obey the same rule. Optional second stage: rescore the ~6k fork nodes with DaughterNet (only 7 evaluable fork parents have p in the current export) and drop forks whose triple score is below a threshold picked on the public-calibrated objective 1.36*dTP - 0.36*dForks_eval > 0.
hypotheses.upper_bound: Removing all 43 FP forks with no TP loss would give local J 23/151 = 0.152 (+0.0033 score). Public, under the assumed TP 19 / FP 13 / FN 21: J 0.358 -> 19/40 = 0.475 (+0.012). The mid rule reaches only 11 of 43 local FP (26%), so its public ceiling is ~3-4 FP forks: J 19/50 = 0.38 (+0.002).
hypotheses.lab_test: Measured on exp39's final graph (scratchpad/div_audit7.py, fork labels equal to official 23/43). mid >= 4.0 removes 369 forks: 358 free, 11 FP, 0 TP; local J +0.0071, so +0.0007 score. mid >= 3.5 removes 16 FP and 1 TP (+0.0005). mid >= 3.0 removes 22 FP and 4 TP: -0.0008 locally, but positive under the public calibration. Embryo split: 44b6 has only 1-2 of the removed FP, so the per-embryo +0.001 gate will likely fail on 44b6. Next: add a 'forkmid' tail step to replay.py and run SELECTION then CONFIRMATION on exp48-equivalent (div_insert forks included). Success: 0 TP lost on both embryos, score >= +0.0005, and a positive public-calibrated objective. Ship only inside a bundle.
hypotheses.expected_gain: Local +0.0005..+0.0008 (measured: 11 FP forks x ~0.0065 J each). Public: each removed FP fork gives dJ ~ J/(D-1) = 0.36/52 = 0.0069, i.e. +0.0007 score. 1-3 such forks gives +0.0007..+0.002.
hypotheses.transfer_risk: Low to medium. The rule is model-free geometry. However, GT mid has p90 5.2 um, so some real divisions are asymmetric, and on the public embryo a TP fork with mid >= 4 could be lost. The safety margin is thin (TP max 3.8 um), so use 4.0 or 4.5, not 3.5. The coord-head port shifts coordinates by up to 2 um and needs a re-check.
hypotheses.not_closed_because: exp36 hygiene (sister floor 5 um + already-divided filter) and the DivNet veto use different signals. The safe-div knob sweeps closed on 2026-09-11 covered existing gates on 12 videos with 14 divisions. This is a NEW gate (parent-to-midpoint / angle), measured with official-equivalent fork labels on all 199 videos (66 evaluable forks).

hypotheses.mechanism: div_insert (exp48) runs post-tail, after the short-track filter (MIN_TRACK_LEN 6) and linefit. A second daughter whose orphan track is shorter than 6 frames is already deleted when the insertion looks for it. Between the ckpt (the safe-div input) and the final graph, the number of GT divisions with no second-daughter node rises from 13 to 23, so ~10 divisions (6.6%) lose their daughter to the tail. Once forked, OUTPUT_KEEP_DIVISION_COMPONENTS=1 would have protected them. Separately, 12 missed divisions have the second daughter claimed by an unscored relink edge (edge_prob 0). The edge filter (probe 29) drops such edges only when the ILP linked elsewhere. The ILP has ZERO forks (0 of 1.46M solution edges on 67 sampled videos), so it never re-links the daughter to its parent, and the freed daughter is left as an orphan that only a post-ef insertion can take.
hypotheses.change: Add a DaughterNet insertion pass at the safe-division slot (ckpt graph, orphans of any track length, same tools/div_insert.py code path, cap 2 per video, steal branch off). Its forks then survive the short-track filter via KEEP_DIVISION_COMPONENTS. Keep the existing post-tail pass, ordered after edgefilter, as the pass for daughters freed by the edge filter. DaughterNet p is needed for short-track nodes that are missing from the 1M export: rescore with K-DN-score (one short Kaggle GPU run).
hypotheses.upper_bound: 22 local GT divisions (10 tail-deleted + 12 p=0 claims), 14.6% of GT. All TP at zero FP would give J 45/194 = 0.232, i.e. +0.011 local score. At a realistic 30% recall and 40% precision, +7 TP and +10 FP give J 30/(30+53+121) = 0.147, i.e. +0.0028 local.
hypotheses.lab_test: Add a stage=ckpt option to replay.py's insertion (the replay already runs ckpt -> safe divisions -> tail). Export triples from the ckpt graphs, score the new nodes with experiments/l2_daughternet/kdn_score (Kaggle T4, ~30 min), then run a SELECTION grid (threshold, cap 1/2/3), then ONE CONFIRMATION vs exp48-equivalent (and vs exp48+ef if probe 29 transfers). Success: net TP >= +3, added-fork precision >= 0.35, score >= +0.001, each embryo >= +0.0005, node ratio change < +0.1%.
hypotheses.transfer_risk: Medium. Short daughter tracks are also where detector noise lives, so precision may be lower than for long orphans. The post-ef half depends on probe 29 transferring. It keeps a few more nodes (node multiplier up by < 0.01%).

This is not a relink knob.

hypotheses.mechanism: No stage of the shipped stack uses the one learned PAIRWISE signal for the second daughter. The ILP at division weight 1.2 outputs ZERO forks (measured: 0 nodes with 2 successors in the raw solution graphs, 67/199 videos sampled). The relink is 1:1 Hungarian. Safe-div ranks by parent_dist + 0.15*sister, and div_insert multiplies node-level DaughterNet probabilities. The candidate-pair score p(u->v) of the SimpleNodeTransformer, trained on GT edges that include the 302 division edges, is discarded because only ILP solution edges are kept (the raw geff stores solution edges only). B20's diagnosis was that a parent-level score cannot resolve WHICH candidate is the daughter, and the L2 steal rule decides with the claimer's own edge_prob < 0.3. Claims are the largest miss class: 54 of 132, with claimer edges of median p 0.71 and a median step of 1.65 um, so p(u->v) vs p(w->v) is the natural arbiter.
hypotheses.change: Kernel: keep the full candidate-edge probability dict from the edge transformer (before the ILP) and pass it to div_insert. Triple score = p_par(u) * p_dau(v) * p_dau(c1)^alpha * p_edge(u->v)^beta. The steal branch requires p_edge(u->v) >= p_edge(w->v) + margin instead of p(w->v) < 0.3. Add a parent-level feature: the second-best outgoing p_edge of u to t+1 at sister geometry. Code change is only in div_insert plus one dict capture in the predictor script.
hypotheses.upper_bound: Pool as in the L2 steal confirmation: 15 added forks, 4 TP (precision 27%, which is public break-even). Precision 50% at the same TP count gives public dJ = (0.5*1.36-0.36)*n/D = 0.32*4/53 = +0.024, i.e. +0.0024. If a third of the 54 claimed misses became reachable at 50% precision: local +18 forks and +9 TP give J 32/(32+52+119) = 0.158, i.e. +0.004 local.
hypotheses.lab_test: Run one GPU kernel (Kaggle 2xT4, ~1-1.5 h) that dumps candidate-edge probabilities for the 64 SELECTION videos and join them into replay.py (div_insert reads them). Grid beta in {0, 0.5, 1} and steal margin in {0, 0.1, 0.2}. For CONFIRMATION, dump the 135 remaining videos (~2-3 GPU h). Success: added-fork precision >= 0.40 with TP >= exp48's insertion on confirmation, score >= +0.001 over exp48, each embryo >= +0.0005.
hypotheses.expected_gain: Local +0.001..+0.003 (optimistic, because the edge network is in-sample). Public +0.0005..+0.0025, but only if probe 29 shows the edge network's probabilities transfer to the hidden embryo.
hypotheses.transfer_risk: High. The edge network was trained on all 199 train videos, so its p(u->v) is in-sample in the lab, like the relink-off change that won locally and lost 0.002 on the LB. Gate the line on probe 29 (edge filter that trusts ILP/edge-net choices): pursue only if exp49 >= ~0.951.
hypotheses.not_closed_because: B22 listed the learned edge score as division evidence, but it was never measured. The closed division lines are the DivNet veto (node-level), the pair model B32 (closed at the reach audit), clustering, and synthetic/dorado data. The ILP division-weight probes (1.2 -> 0.9) do not matter here because the relink replaces the ILP edge set.
